articles.title: Volcanic Rock
articles.summary: Flat semi-matte surface with a fine even grain, like pitted stone; no metal flake, soft dull sheen in whatever colour you give it. Reads as your plain colour in a dry semi-matte, with a faint uneven sheen like rough stone; no grain is visible.
articles.what: Up close: Takes your colour. The paint is flat; the texture is in roughness only, broad blotchy patches roughly 60-150 px, as dull and slightly less dull areas (R 154, std 15). Metal is zero and clearcoat is a flat dull 220, so it is a dry stone-like surface, not a pitted grain. From a distance: Reads as your plain colour in a dry semi-matte, with a faint uneven sheen like rough stone; no grain is visible. Measured spec (average): metal 23, roughness 154, coat 220. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: none. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, show car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Volcanic Rock on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: matte rock is meant to cover everything
Hood and roof: broad flat panels show the blotches
Numbers read fine; there is no texture to disturb them. Use light colours on dark rock.
Fine grain or sand patterns: adds the pitted stone look the base lacks
Pairs well with: matte black, rust, copper, dark grey.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a visible stone texture: the roughness patches are broad and soft, no pitting at 1:1
Not metallic: metal is 0 and sparkle 0
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to glossy finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 23 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 154 (semi-matte), clearcoat 220 (almost no clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to glossy finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine grain or sand patterns: adds the pitted stone look the base lacks; camo or mottle patterns: for a rock and lava look
Patterns to avoid: glitter or flake patterns: kills the dry stone feel; glossy stripe patterns: clash with the dull surface
Spec overlays that work: pebble or grain spec overlays: makes the stone texture visible; matte-to-satin mottle: stronger rock feel
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
